THE REPORT’S OWN FUNNEL

It counts organisations, not pilots.

03 / 29
The 95 per cent counts organisations with no return, not pilots. The report then relabelled it a failure rate, though its own funnel is milder.
Evaluated a tool60%
Reached a pilot20%
Reached production5%

The report measured something narrower than the headline. Ninety-five per cent of organisations were getting zero return, not ninety-five per cent of pilots. Its own funnel proves the point: sixty per cent evaluated a tool, twenty per cent piloted, five per cent reached production. On those numbers the pilot failure rate is seventy-five per cent, twenty points milder than the figure in circulation.

The document then relabelled its own result a ninety-five per cent failure rate, one paragraph later. Three things belong on the record. It defines success as something remarked upon, not measured. Its sample was fifty-two organisations and a hundred and fifty-three leaders at four conferences. It calls itself preliminary findings.
